originalPromptSet.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. One independent premium near-realistic biology atlas rendering with fine organic tissue detail, restrained translucent cytoplasm and clear three-dimensional soft light on ivory background. Not cartoon or vector icons. NO text, Chinese, labels, numerals, arrows, symbols or boxes. This is educational cellular enlargement, not a microscope photograph. Subject: Euglena gracilis-like SINGLE cell: elongated spindle-shaped body with a rounded anterior and gently pointed posterior, thin flexible pellicle bearing subtle longitudinal/spiral strips, not thick cellulose cell wall. Several green lens/disc-like chloroplasts inside cytoplasm, one pale central nucleus, small pale paramylon grains, small anterior reservoir and one red-orange pigment eyespot near its base in cytoplasm, not an eyeball or a chloroplast. ONE long external flagellum emerges from the anterior reservoir/canal; never draw many flagella around body or a flagellum from posterior. Complete cell and entire long external flagellum fit comfortably within frame. Pale aqueous background, three-quarter view, enough transparency to see chloroplasts but no false bright rainbow organelles.

Subject: a close enlarged partial cutaway of the MIDDLE BODY of one photosynthetic Euglena. Show gently curved transparent flexible pellicle strips at perimeter, a single pale nucleus, and several realistic green lens-shaped chloroplasts embedded separately in granular cytoplasm with some small pale storage granules. Chloroplasts should clearly be intracellular green organelles, not leaves or whole smaller cells. Do not turn cell perimeter into a thick plant wall. No complicated chloroplast interior or invented thylakoid stacks, no eyespot in this middle-body crop. Crop clearly as an enlarged cellular detail rather than whole organism. No labels or leader lines.
